Event Theme & Keepsakes · design v1.0 + Full Set amendment (11–17) · 30 Sep 2026 · awaiting human visual approval

One event look,
carried everywhere.

The host gives the event its identity once: an image, a color, a hashtag. FiveFrames carries it onto guest screens, five keepsake styles and four signage formats. Nobody edits a layout. Sample photography is illustrated (no stock images). Every render on this board uses the real FiveFrames logo geometry, the brand fonts and the Satori-compatible template structure. Sections 00–10 are the accepted v1.0 design. Sections 11–17 are the Full Set amendment: a second keepsake family of five styles, made from all five of a guest’s photos.

00

The two moments

Top: a themed event, where the host’s image, color and hashtag suddenly make everything theirs. Bottom: an event whose host changed nothing, which is a first-class state, not a fallback.

Seven curated colors, no custom picker in MVP. Each key maps to fixed, pre-verified roles (every pairing above clears WCAG AA: fill/text ≥ 4.88, ink on white ≥ 5.62, onDark on night ≥ 7.16). Marigold is the one light color: its buttons use ink text instead of darkening the fill, so it still looks like marigold. Hosts only ever see the swatch and its label. The adjustment is never shown. Host chrome, the Operator Console, the QR plate and the FiveFrames mark are never themed.

390 · Settings → Look (full scroll)

Event header with the theme image, event tabs, then Look sub-tabs. The same controls, and Save at the end (the existing mobile pattern).

What moved, and why (presentation only)

Look is only the look

Create → Look holds theme image, color, hashtag and welcome. It also holds the guest keepsakes toggle (the existing sharing setting), because that is where its effect is visible. Reveal timing and gallery visibility move to Create → Details as an “After the party” card. They are the same fields with the same defaults. The wizard still has three steps.

Settings gets three sub-sections

Event & gallery (details, reveal, visibility) · Look (the studio) · Links. Each is its own form with the existing unsaved-changes guard. Switching sub-section with unsaved edits asks first, the same as leaving the page.

Two save models, stated plainly

The theme image uploads and saves immediately (architecture §7a begin → commit → swap). Its tile says “Saved”. Remove confirms first. Everything else waits for Save changes. The hint under Unsaved changes explains the effect without technical language: “Applies to guest screens, keepsakes and signage from now on. Signage you’ve printed keeps working.”

Stale copy replaced

“Printed on the share cards guests create” → “Printed on keepsakes and signage…”. “Lets guests share a FiveFrames card…” → the Guest keepsakes copy.

Print · preselected

The FiveFrames printed photo from the marketing site, made into a keepsake. White paper, the photo contained with even margins, and a caption lip holding the message, the event name in Fraunces, and date + hashtag beside the brand lockup. Theme image: not used. It is the calmest style and right for any event or photo, which is why it’s preselected. Accent: the date square and the hashtag.

Booth

Photobooth energy: the whole canvas in the event color, a letter-spaced date stamp and hashtag across the top, the photo in a white keyline print, and the event name at the foot. Theme image: not used. The color is the theme. Never shows the message, so it stays a pure booth print. Mark is one colour (white, or ink on marigold).

Poster

The event as a headline. The theme image is a background field across the top (cover crop, biased to the upper third, with a night gradient for legibility). The name sits over it in Fraunces 84. The guest’s photo is a print overlapping the field edge, so it is always the largest object. No image: night with an accent glow, the same field as the guest header.

Journal

Editorial. A masthead row with the theme image as a cropped 112px motif plate (dropped when absent: the text simply starts at the margin), a heavy ink rule, then the photo. Portrait photos get a side column: the message as a Fraunces pull-quote, or with no message, the day as a large accent numeral. Landscape anchors the same block at the foot.

Album

Warm and tactile. A white-bordered print tilted −2.5° on the event’s tint, with a small label card (+1.6°) holding the message, name and date. The theme image becomes a derived texture: cover-cropped at 12% opacity under the tint. With no image the tint is flat, and it still reads as colored paper.

Shared rules (all five)

Canvas 1080 × 1350 (4:5): the Instagram feed ratio, and it fits a phone gallery. The photo is contained: no style crops the guest’s photo, and each window sizes itself to the photo’s own ratio. The theme image never touches the photo. Text sizes step down by length, then clamp (name 2 lines, message 2 lines, or 8 in Journal’s side column). Minimum type on canvas is 24px, about 8.5px at a 360px-wide phone view. No display name, link, QR or count is ever an input.

Brandmark

The horizontal lockup at 30px (≈2.8% of canvas width), always on the border or field, never on the photo. Placement: in the caption row (Print) or the bottom-right corner (Booth, Poster, Journal, Album). Tones come only from the identity: onLight on white/tint, white one-colour on accent/night fields, ink one-colour on marigold. The brand violet centre is not themed. No slogan, URL or call to action.

Satori subset

These renders use only what next/og supports: flex and absolute boxes, border-radius, box-shadow, linear/radial gradients, object-fit/position, opacity, 2D rotate. No grid, filters, blend modes or masks. The fonts are the bundled Fraunces 600 and Jakarta 500/600/700/800 TTFs, and no italic is needed. The board’s HTML for each style is a direct spec.

07

Guest · Choose a style → Share or save (mobile)

Lightweight on purpose: one screen, one choice. States 3–10 cover preparing, ready, cancel, failure, save-only and saved.

Guest-flow rules

Where it lives

Only in the guest’s own view: completion rows, the “Your photos” list on closed/return visits, and the own-photo viewer. Never in capture, preview-before-commit, Your Five slots or the gallery (for anyone). Hosts and gallery viewers get no keepsake action.

One step

Choose a style → Share or Save. Five thumbnails in one row (all visible at 360px; each is the real template on the guest’s photo), one large stage, swipe on the stage as a shortcut. Share and Save keepsake both open the same picker.

Original vs keepsake

Said three ways, with no technical terms: the viewer’s two labelled groups, the picker’s subtitle (“A new image made from your photo. Your original stays exactly as you took it.”), and the file itself (fiveframes-{event}-{style}.jpg).

Bytes before the tap

On open and on every selection, fetch the selected style’s JPEG. Share is enabled only when the bytes are in hand. Save works without them (?download=1 navigation).

Motion

On open, the photo settles into the preselected style (240ms, ease-settle). Style changes cross-fade in 160ms. Reduced motion: instant.

09

Themed signage family

Four formats that share one system (field + white scan side + fixed QR plate) and are composed differently for how each is used.

FormatCanvas / printQR & quiet zoneTheme imageHierarchyPhysical notes
QR600 × 720 · 5 × 6 in, or any size336 units (29–33 modules) · plate pad = 4 modulesNeverName → QR → instruction → reassurance. Hashtag top-right. A 16-unit accent band at the foot.For placements where the code must dominate (stickers, desks, doors). At 5 × 6 in the QR is 7 cm.
Table card700 × 500 · 7 × 5 in landscape212 units ≈ 5.4 cmLeft 280-unit panel (cover, 50% 35%)The panel carries the identity: lockup, name, date, hashtag. The white side is only for scanning.Close range (30–60 cm). 0.125 in bleed on the panel edge, 0.25 in safe area. Body text ≥ 13 units ≈ 9.4 pt.
Poster1200 × 1800 · 24 × 36 in (2:3)540 units ≈ 27 cm → scans from ~2.7 mTop 780-unit fieldName in Fraunces 108 → QR → “Scan. You have five frames.” in Jakarta 800 56. The hierarchy reads from across a room.Content stays inside a 6% inset, so an A-series print (1 : 1.414, scaled to width) trims only the field and the band.
Digital1920 × 1080 (16:9)520 units ≈ 48% of heightLeft 1040-unit fieldName very large on the field. QR + instruction on white. Built for a TV, projector or tablet on a stand.Everything within a 5% title-safe inset for TV overscan. A landscape image previews fine in a group chat. Not a scaled poster.

The QR plate is never themed

Ink modules on a white plate. Plate padding = 4 modules at every size. Nothing inside the plate. Accent brackets sit outside it (a gap ≥ 9 units), so they never enter the quiet zone. The plate always rests on white, never on the theme image. This fixes today’s renderer, which draws brackets inside the plate padding and pads with under 4 modules.

Low-quality or busy theme images

They only ever appear as a field behind white text, under a night gradient (0.15 → 0.92). They are never behind the QR or the instruction. Under 1600px the host sees the “may print soft” note. A poor image degrades to a soft background, never to an illegible sign.

Copy is fixed

“Scan. You have five frames.” · “No app. No account.” Hosts can’t edit these, the QR destination or the layout (product.md §11.3).

Long names

Fraunces sizes step down (e.g. poster 108 → 92 → 76 → 64), then wrap to 2 lines (poster), 3 (table card, digital) or 2 (QR), with an ellipsis as a last resort. A hashtag that doesn’t fit beside the date drops to its own line.

10

Signage preview: Draft vs activated

The host always sees what they’ll get. Before payment, nothing on screen can work as a code.

OverviewGuest screensKeepsakesSignage
Live preview
QRTable cardPosterDigital
Draft preview
Table card · 7 × 5 in landscape. Close-range scanning at a table or desk. The code here is a placeholder. Your real QR and downloads arrive when you activate.

Draft / pending payment

A Draft preview badge where Download will be. The placeholder is a dot field with no finder patterns, so it can’t decode and doesn’t look like a working code. It reads PREVIEW / Not a working code, with the same footprint, so the layout is exact. There is no download affordance anywhere, and a screenshot contains nothing that admits anyone.

OverviewGuest screensKeepsakesSignage
Live preview
QRTable cardPosterDigital
Download table card
Table card · 7 × 5 in landscape. Close-range scanning at a table or desk. Uses your event’s real QR. Changing the look never changes where it points.

Activated

The same preview with the event’s real QR, plus a dark host-utility Download button per format (existing route, unchanged). The note reminds the host that theme changes never move the QR.

Where signage lives

Create → Look and Settings → Look (Signage tab) in every editable state. After activation, Create · Share (“You’re all set”) keeps its QR + link hand-off and links to the Signage tab for the four formats. It no longer says “poster and phone-screen version are on your dashboard”.

Why each exists

Signature

The brandmark’s construction, made of photographs. The one composition only FiveFrames can own. It reads as “five moments, one shape” to someone who has never seen the logo.

Strip

The photobooth ritual: a sequence you read top to bottom, as a paper object laid on the event. The one people recognise instantly.

Grid

Equal weight. No moment is bigger than another. It is also the most forgiving crop in the family, because every slot is within 4% of square.

Spotlight

Hierarchy: a lead picture and four that follow, like a photo essay. Photo 1 leads because order is commit order. The guest never picks a hero.

Prints

Objecthood. Five instant-style prints on a surface, each at its own small tilt. Square windows, so it never favours an orientation.

SameDifferent

12

Signature · built from the mark

The preselected Full Set style is the FiveFrames symbol made of the guest’s five photographs: landscape, portrait, landscape, portrait, turning clockwise around a closing square. No four corners meet. Slot n is SYMBOL_FRAMES[n], so capture 5, the last one kept, fills the centre, and the centre carries the colour, as it does in the mark.

The mark · 120 units

Four 76 × 36 frames and a 32 × 32 centre on a 120 square, with 8-unit gutters (lib/brand/logo.ts). Order is SYMBOL_FRAMES: 1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 left, 5 centre.

A · Literal

The mark scaled up. Arms are 2.11 : 1. A portrait photo in a landscape arm keeps 35% of its height; a landscape photo in a portrait arm keeps 35% of its width.

Rejected · crops too hard
B · Square, thin gutters

The same arm length and centre, with gutters narrowed to 24 px. Arms become 1.84 : 1, so a portrait photo keeps 41% of its height in slots 1 and 3.

Rejected · still starves slots 1, 3
C · Chosen

Portrait arms keep the mark’s exact 36 : 76. Landscape arms open to 3 : 2, because phone photos are mostly portrait and those arms receive them most. A portrait photo keeps 50% of its height, faces included. The form becomes 6 : 7.

Signature geometry
On the 1200 × 1800 canvas
Leo’s Graduation Party
Fri, 29 May 2026
12345
Slot rectangles (canvas px, commit order)
#Slotx, yw × hratioFrom
1Landscape · top72, 72672 × 4481.500Mark frame 1
2Portrait · right768, 72360 × 7600.474Mark frame 2
3Landscape · bottom456, 856672 × 4481.500Mark frame 3
4Portrait · left72, 544360 × 7600.474Mark frame 4
5Square · closing456, 544288 × 2881.000Mark centre

Form 1056 × 1232 at (72, 72). Gutter 24. Portrait arm = (1056 − 2·24 − 288) / 2 = 360. Landscape arm = 360 + 24 + 288 = 672 long, 672 / 1.5 = 448 high. Accent mat: 10 px around slot 5, inside its gutter.

What stays exactly the mark

Topology and handedness (clockwise, landscape first). No four corners meet: every junction is a T. The fifth region is square, sits where the mark’s centre sits, and is the only one in colour. The portrait arms keep 36:76.

What is refined for photographs

Gutters drop from 8/120 of the form to 24 px, so the photos, not the paper, draw the shape. Landscape arms open from 2.11 : 1 to 3 : 2. The corner radius drops from the mark’s 7/36 to 4 px, because photographs want nearly sharp prints. The form becomes 6 : 7 instead of square, which leaves the 2:3 canvas a caption row instead of an empty third.

Colour lives in the centre

Slot 5 sits on a 10 px mat in the event’s base colour (violet by default), inside its gutter, with 14 px of paper still between it and its neighbours. It is the style’s only accent besides the date square. The accent never touches a photo.

A restrained maker’s mark

Because the photographs already draw the symbol, Signature carries the wordmark only (28 px, onLight), at the right of the caption row. It is the one style without the full lockup.

Caption row

In the 496 px below the form, vertically centred: optional theme seal (128 px circle), then the Fraunces name (80 → 66 → 56 → 48 by length, 2 lines), then the accent square + date + hashtag (Jakarta 30). The wordmark sits at the right on the same centre line.

Theme image: a seal, not a sixth frame

A 128 px circle beside the name, with a paper ring and a thin tint ring. The shape, the scale and its place in the caption keep it apart from the five rectangles. Without an image the seal is simply absent, and the name starts at the margin.

Test (Slice 16)

Like logo.test.ts: five in-bounds, non-overlapping slots that exactly tile the form with 24 px gutters; slots 1 and 3 have ratio 1.5; 2 and 4 have 36:76; slot 5 is square and centred between 1–4; no point is a corner of four slots.

13

Full Set · theme states

Every style looks finished with a full theme, with only a color, and with nothing set. The theme image has a different role in each style, and it is never a rectangle the size of a capture. It can’t read as a sixth photo: it is a seal, a ground, a band behind type or a texture, or it is absent.

Shared rules (all five)

Canvas 1200 × 1800 (2:3), 2.16 MP

Exactly a 4 × 6 in print at 300 ppi, the standard photo and booth sheet. Tall enough that five photos each have real area on a phone. It shows whole in Messages, WhatsApp, Stories and the camera roll. Instagram’s feed crops anything taller than 4:5, which is an accepted tradeoff.

Photos

Cover crop, focus 50% 30%. Nothing is ever drawn inside a slot. Slot radius 2–4 px. Minimum type on canvas is 27 px (about 8 px on a 360 px phone view).

Text

Name only in Fraunces 600, stepping down by length, then clamped (2–4 lines by style). Date and hashtag in Jakarta. Missing date or hashtag collapses its space. No message, display name, welcome message, per-photo data, QR or URL is an input.

14

Full Set · mixed-orientation pressure tests

The same default event, six real-world sets, every style. Each source is drawn at its true ratio (thumbnails at left, uncropped). Slots use D20’s deterministic cover crop at focus 50% 30%: centred across, 30% from the top when height is trimmed. There is no face detection, and none is needed to pass.

Worst-case share of a photo kept (the trimmed dimension), per style
StyleSlot ratios (w/h)Portrait 3:4Landscape 4:3Tall 9:16Wide 16:9
Signature1.50 · 0.47 · 1.0050%36%38%27%
Strip1.3854%97%41%78%
Grid0.9778%73%58%54%
Spotlight1.00 · 0.8075%60%56%45%
Prints1.0075%75%56%56%

Green ≥ 55% · amber 40–55% · red < 40%. Red appears only in Signature, and only for its less common inputs: a landscape or wide photo in a portrait arm (slots 2, 4 keep 36% / 27% of the width, centred), or a 9:16 photo in a landscape arm (38%, top-biased). The everyday case, a 3:4 portrait, never drops below 50% anywhere in the family. Grid is the robustness benchmark.

What design does about crops

Focus 50% 30%, one family constant

Heads in phone portraits sit roughly 10–45% down. A 3:4 portrait in a 3:2 slot keeps the band from 15% to 65%, and faces survive in every set above. Architecture’s rule (centred, top-biased only when height is trimmed) is exactly CSS object-position: 50% 30%.

No extreme slots except the one we chose

Every slot is between 1 : 2.11 and 3 : 2. Grid and Prints never lose more than 27% of a 3:4 or 4:3 photo, and Spotlight’s lead is square. Only Signature keeps a mark-true extreme (its portrait arms). Its failure is a side crop that keeps the centred subject, never a lost head.

The honest failure

A subject in the bottom quarter of a portrait photo, like the child and the cake in the last row, is cut off in a wide slot (Signature 1, Strip 1). Only content analysis could fix that, and D20 excludes it. The keepsake still looks deliberate, and the original is untouched and downloadable. Accepted, and not something to work around with a crop editor.

14 · Fewer than five, or a photo deleted

The accepted Single-photo picker, exactly as in v1.0: no switch, no hint that another family exists. After a deletion this is permanent.

Picker information architecture

Two families, one switch

A two-segment control, One photo · Your five, above the stage. Each family shows only its own five thumbnails and preselects its own default (Print · Signature). Ten styles never appear together.

The switch exists only when it can be used

It renders only when the server’s availability flag is true (getFullSetSources + sharing on). When the flag is false, the picker is the accepted v1.0 screen, pixel for pixel. There is no disabled segment and no teaser.

Where it opens

From a photo, it opens on One photo (that photo). From “See them together”, it opens on Your five. Switching family keeps the picker open and prepares the new family’s preselected style.

Copy

Family label “Your five”, card title “Your five, together”, action “See them together”. Never “unlock”, “complete”, “5/5”, “reward”, or “Full Set” (an internal and host term). Styles are never called frames.

Stage size at 390

The 2:3 keepsake is about 262 × 393 pt, two-thirds of the screen width, with thumbnails of 58 × 87. The family switch costs 48 pt of stage height. Share and Save stay in the thumb zone.

Motion

As v1.0: settle 240 ms on open, 160 ms cross-fade between styles and between families. Reduced motion: instant.

16

Full Set · guest desktop (1440 · 1280 · 1024)

1440 · Your five, Signature ready

The keepsake is 504 × 756 CSS px on the stage, so every photo can be read. The panel is 400: switch, subtitle, list, then Share and Save pinned to the bottom of the panel.

Desktop rules

Stage

The keepsake height is the viewport minus 120, capped so the panel keeps its width. At 1024 it is still about 420 × 630. It sits on the subtle surface with the print shadow, and the stage never scrolls.

Panel

400 at ≥ 1280 and 380 below. The family switch is the first control. The list rows are thumbnail, name and one line, and the selected row gets a tint, a 1.5 px accent ring and a check (never colour alone). Default is marked “· default”.

Originals

Your five’s originals row says “Original photos · Exactly as you took them” and downloads all five with the existing guest download. Keepsakes and originals stay visibly separate.

Completion

The split shell’s action region gets the same tint card as mobile, placed between the photo cards and Download my photos, which stays the only accent primary.

390 · One photo (accepted)

The same tab on One photo shows the accepted five, unchanged.

Host integration rules

Host words

Hosts see One photo · All five. Guests see One photo · Your five. The switch defaults to One photo (the family every guest can use).

Samples

Five bundled, mixed-orientation illustrated samples in this order: portrait, portrait, landscape, portrait, square. Slot 1 of Signature and Strip therefore always shows a portrait in a landscape slot, so hosts see real crop behaviour. No guest data and no token.

Nothing a guest could reach

No download, share or “make” action exists on the host side for either family. There’s no Portrait/Landscape toggle for All five, because the sample set already mixes orientations.

Sharing off

The whole Keepsakes tab dims with “Guests won’t see these until you turn them on”. That covers both families, because it is one toggle.

Draft

Previews are allowed in every editable state, including Draft. They contain no QR and no link, so nothing changes before activation.

Demo (/demo)

Unchanged by this amendment. The accepted board has no demo keepsake surface. If one is added later, D14 and D20 allow DOM previews of either family on sample photos, with no route calls.
